definitions.explanation: To speak angrily to someone because they have done something wrong. Often used by parents, teachers, or supervisors.

examples.english: I was scolded by my mother.
examples.notes: Passive form {叱|しか}られる is very common

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}が{生徒|せいと}を{叱|しか}った。
{遅刻|ちこく}して{叱|しか}られるかもしれない。
examples.english: I might get scolded for being late.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pattern: Xを{叱|しか}る (scold X).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing action. {叱|しか}っている = 'is scolding.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{子供|こども}を{叱|しか}る (scold a child)
・{叱|しか}られる (be scolded—passive, very common)
・{厳|きび}しく{叱|しか}る (scold harshly)
・{愛情|あいじょう}を{込|こ}めて{叱|しか}る (scold with love)

CONTRAST WITH {怒|おこ}る:
・{叱|しか}る: to scold (corrective, educational purpose)
・{怒|おこ}る: to get angry (emotional reaction)

In theory, {叱|しか}る is done for the other person's benefit, while {怒|おこ}る is simply expressing anger. In practice, these often overlap.

REGISTER: Neutral.
